requirement_text.REQ-418:
MOB-2 authenticates via OIDC Authorization-Code + PKCE through the system browser (flutter_appauth). That needs an OIDC client the app can name. None exists: priv/keycloak/realms/bpm-default.json's only client is letflow-web (publicClient true, directAccessGrantsEnabled true, redirectUris ["*"], webOrigins ["*"]). Reusing letflow-web is rejected: its wildcard redirect list would let any app that registers any scheme receive a mobile authorization code, and its password grant has no place on a device. THIS IS A SECURITY CHANGE. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a required gate (identity configuration plus a public, unauthenticated response shape; docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md).

PART 1 -- the client, in priv/keycloak/realms/bpm-default.json: clientId "letflow-mobile"; publicClient true; standardFlowEnabled true; directAccessGrantsEnabled false; implicitFlowEnabled false; serviceAccountsEnabled false; attributes "pkce.code.challenge.method": "S256" (Keycloak then rejects an authorization request without an S256 challenge) and "post.logout.redirect.uris": "com.bizdala.letflow:/oauth2redirect"; redirectUris exactly ["com.bizdala.letflow:/oauth2redirect"] -- no "*", no http(s) URI, no trailing wildcard; webOrigins [] (a native app makes no CORS requests). Protocol mappers: the same realm-roles mapper letflow-web carries (claim.name "roles" -- Letflow reads that claim), plus an oidc-audience-mapper with included.client.audience "letflow-web" and access.token.claim "true". The audience mapper is NOT optional: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc validates with Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3, whose verify_aud_claim (deps/oidcc/src/oidcc_token.erl:1283) rejects any access token whose aud lacks the configured :oidc client_id ("letflow-web", config/dev.exs:97, config/test.exs:128). This is exactly ISS-0275's defect (lib/letflow/design/iss0275-audience-mapper-fix.md) and must not be reintroduced for the second client. validate_jwt does not check azp, so azp "letflow-mobile" is accepted. Do NOT modify the letflow-web client. The redirect scheme must equal the Android applicationId REQ-419 creates (com.bizdala.letflow; see the S9 header's open question).

PART 2 -- how the app learns the client_id. DECIDED HERE (with the reasoning below; REQ-VALIDATOR/REVIEWER may overturn): add a sixth key "client_id" to GET /api/mobile/tenant-config, valued System.get_env("MOBILE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID") || "letflow-mobile" -- the same env-then-constant shape Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig already uses for the web SPA's client_id (lib/letflow/routers/tenant_config.ex:168 and :361, OIDC_CLIENT_ID || "letflow-web"). Security reasoning, to be restated in the moduledoc: (i) an OAuth public-client identifier is not a secret (RFC 6749 §2.2; a public client has no credential), and the web endpoint already publishes its equivalent unauthenticated; (ii) the value is platform-global, not tenant-derived -- byte-identical on every never-error branch (resolvable slug, unknown slug, missing ?slug=, lookup failure) -- so it adds zero enumeration signal, the same status environment_kind has; (iii) the alternative, compiling the id into the app, would work today but freezes it into every shipped build, so a deployment whose realms register the client under another name, or a later rename, would need an app release; server-sent keeps the one-tenant-agnostic-build constraint without that coupling. (It does NOT support a per-tenant client name -- the value is platform-global by design, point ii; per-tenant naming would be a new requirement and a new disclosure analysis.) CONTRACT CHANGE TO CALL OUT: the module's moduledoc says "It returns exactly five keys" and "Adding a sixth key to this response is a security change, not a feature"; REQ-124's and REQ-282's exact-shape tests in test/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config_test.exs assert five keys. Update the table, the "What this endpoint discloses" section and the per-field-variance paragraph to six keys, and update the exact-shape assertions to the new six-key set -- never loosen them to a subset check. Also record the change in lib/letflow/design/req124-mobile-tenant-config.md as a dated addendum.

OUT OF SCOPE: provisioning letflow-mobile into per-tenant realms other than bpm-default (Letflow does not provision Keycloak realms or clients programmatically -- lib/letflow/routers/onboarding.ex's moduledoc lists realm/client provisioning as not done); any apps/mobile/ code; the web endpoint.

task.description: Design the two parts of REQ-418 (branch feature/WF02-REQ418-20260927 already created and pushed by ORCH; verify it out with `git branch --show-current` before writing). PART 1: the new public PKCE-S256 letflow-mobile Keycloak client in priv/keycloak/realms/bpm-default.json, exact attribute/redirectUris/webOrigins/mapper shape per the requirement text, with an explicit note that letflow-web must remain byte-identical. PART 2: the sixth `client_id` key on GET /api/mobile/tenant-config (lib/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config.ex), env-then-constant resolution, and the moduledoc/table/disclosure-section/exact-shape-test updates the contract change requires. Write the design to lib/letflow/design/req418-mobile-oidc-client.md. Design only -- no implementation code, no realm JSON edits, no route/test edits.
